content: The intranasal administration of metoclopramide can interact with various drugs, leading to significant pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic effects. These interactions may necessitate the avoidance of concurrent use or the selection of alternative therapeutic agents. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions: 1. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Clonazepam: The combination of these drugs can enhance the effects of one another. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. The use of metoclopramide intranasally should be avoided depending on the clinical importance of the interacting drug for the patient. 2. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Clonidine: Co-administration may increase the effects of both drugs. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. The decision should be based on the clinical necessity of the drugs for the patient. 3. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Clozapine: Clozapine increases the toxicity of metoclopramide via pharmacodynamic synergy. This combination can lead to additive effects, including a higher risk of tardive dyskinesia, extrapyramidal symptoms, and neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Cocaine (topical): Cocaine can increase the levels or effects of metoclopramide by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Concurrent use is not recommended as the metoclopramide dose cannot be adjusted. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Codeine: The combination may enhance the effects of both drugs. Avoid concurrent use or consider alternative therapies. The clinical importance of the drugs should guide the decision. 6. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Crofelemer: Crofelemer may decrease the systemic absorption of metoclopramide by impairing gastrointestinal motility. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects of metoclopramide and adjust treatment as necessary. 7. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Cyclobenzaprine: Co-administration may increase the effects of both drugs. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. The decision should depend on the clinical importance of the drugs for the patient. 8. Metoclopramide (intranasal) and Cyclosporine: Metoclopramide may increase the absorption of cyclosporine. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations and adjust the cyclosporine dose as needed. 9.
